newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-SRI LANKA FACE MAMMOTH DEFICIT VS NZ.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRI LANKA FACE MAMMOTH DEFICIT VS NZ.

text.p: Sri Lanka surrendered to a huge first-innings deficit when they were dismissed just before tea on the third day of the first cricket test against New Zealand at Carisbrook on Sunday.
Sri Lanka were bundled out for 222, 364 runs behind New Zealand's first innings effort of 586 for seven declared.
New Zealand seam bowler Simon Doull lead the destruction with a haul of five for 58.

Fast bowler Heath Davis finished with his test-best figures of three for 34, in his third test, after he hastened Sri Lanka's demise with the second new ball immediately after the drinks break in the second session.

His second delivery of the spell was short and fast, and Pramodya Wickremasinghe, who had hit out lustily to make 43, ducked to avoid it. But he left his bat in the air and the ball clipped it before ballooning to wicketkeeper Adam Parore.

Sri Lanka resumed on 78 for four this morning and reached lunch on 150 for seven. Hashan Tillekaratne, who was left unbeaten on 55, and Wickremasinghe added 73 in 77 minutes for the eighth wicket before Wickremasinghe departed.

Davis then accounted for Nuwan Zoysa, who was caught in the slips, before Doull picked up his fifth wicket when Muttiah Muralitharan scooped a ball in the air to mid-off where Chris Cairns took an easy catch. Not surprisingly, New Zealand captain Stephen Fleming enforced the follow-on.
However, heavy rain started falling during the tea break and play may be abandoned for the day.
